title: That Pineapple Tallow Balm I Keep By the Sink
body:
Okay so. I was just putting some of that tallow balm on my hands. The pineapple one. It was like 11:47pm, I was washing a pan from dinner, and my knuckles were doing that tight, dry thing they do. You know the thing. I grabbed the little jar from the windowsill. The one that’s always there now, next to the sponge. Opened it. And for a second, I wasn’t in my kitchen looking at a pile of dishes. I was… somewhere else. Not a fancy perfume somewhere else. Just a better one. It smells like pineapple. But not the fake candy kind. Not the cleaner kind. Just… pineapple. Good pineapple. The kind you get on vacation when you don’t have to think about anything. That’s the whole point of this, I guess. This **pineapple tallow balm** isn’t magic skin potion. It’s beef fat. I know how that sounds. But it works. And the smell makes using beef fat on your face feel less weird and more like a tiny, two-second holiday.

My hands don’t crack anymore. That’s the big thing. I used to get those little splits at the corners of my thumbs every winter, and they’d hang around into spring. Annoying. Stingy. I tried everything in tubes. Then I saw this **scented tallow balm** on Etsy, of all places. A shop in France makes it. Whipped beef tallow. Grass-fed, all that. I was skeptical. Beef fat? For my face? It sounded like something my great-grandmother might have used, not me. But the reviews were nuts. And they had a pineapple scent. I like pineapple. So I figured, what’s the worst that could happen? I’d be out thirty bucks and have a weird story.

## Why I Even Tried Beef Tallow on My Skin

Look. I’m not a skincare person. I have a face wash. Sometimes I remember moisturizer. My routine is basically “try not to fall asleep with makeup on.” But my skin has moods. It gets dry patches. My elbows are a disaster zone. And my hands, like I said, were a lost cause. I’d bought this stupidly expensive cream from one of those fancy stores last year. Came in a heavy jar. Felt nice. Did nothing. Absolutely nothing. My skin drank it and asked for more. So the idea of using tallow, which is basically rendered beef suet, seemed… logical? In a gross way? But the science-ish part, the part I read when I was procrastinating buying it, made sense. Human skin oil, sebum, has a similar makeup to tallow. So it absorbs. Like, really absorbs. It doesn’t just sit on top playing dress-up. It goes in. My skin was thirsty. Maybe it wanted something familiar. Something… animal-based. That sounds intense. But it’s not. It’s just balm.

Anyway. I ordered the **natural pineapple skincare** thing. The Whipped Tallow Balm. It arrived in a little box. Cute jar. I opened it in my living room, sitting on the floor because I was also untangling a phone charger. First impression? The texture was weird. Good weird. It’s whipped, so it’s not greasy-hard. It’s like… cool butter that’s been all fluffed up. You scoop a tiny bit with your finger and it just… yields. Then you rub it between your palms and it melts. Actually melts. Into nothing. Or into your skin, I guess. And the smell hits you. Not in a punchy way. It just arrives. Pineapple. Summer. That’s it. No “hints of coconut blossom” or “undertones of exotic driftwood.” Just a cheerful, sweet fruit smell that makes you think of poolside drinks even if you’re just on your couch with a knotted cable.

## What This Pineapple Tallow Balm Actually Does

So how do I use it? All the time. That’s the answer. It lives by the kitchen sink. After I wash my hands, I do a tiny dab. The dry, tight feeling is just gone. Not masked. Gone. I keep a smaller jar on my bedside table. If I remember before bed, I’ll put a little on my face. Especially now that it’s spring and the air is being all indecisive—warm one day, windy and dry the next. My face gets confused. This balm doesn’t confuse it. It just… hydrates. I’ve used it on my elbows. My knees. My heels. I put it on my lips once when I couldn’t find my chapstick. Worked fine. Better than fine.

Here’s a thing. I got a small cut on my hand from a can lid. Just a little slice. It healed, but the skin around it was all red and irritated and scaly for days. Like it forgot how to be skin. I put this tallow balm on it. Not on the cut, but around it. The scaly patch was gone in two days. Flat. Normal. I don’t know why. I’m not a doctor. I just know it happened. My partner, who thinks all my skincare experiments are hilarious, even stole some for his eczema patch on his arm. He won’t admit it helped, but he stopped scratching it. And the jar is emptier. So.

The scent is the best part, though. The functional part is the tallow. It mimics sebum, absorbs deep, all that. But the pineapple scent is the experience. It turns a maintenance task—moisturizing—into a tiny moment of pleasure. You’re not slathering on medical-grade goo. You’re having a brief, cheerful interaction with a jar that smells like a Dole Whip from Disneyland. It’s not perfume. It doesn’t linger for hours on your skin. It’s just there for the application, a little “hey, this is nice” signal to your brain. It makes the whole concept feel less clinical and more enjoyable. I look forward to using it. That’s weird to say about a balm. But I do. After a shower. Before bed. When my hands feel like parchment. It’s my little two-second tropical escape in a jar.

## My Skin Now vs. Before

I’m on my second jar now. I ordered another one last week because I saw the first one was getting low and I had a minor panic. I don’t want to be without it. That’s the real review, right? Repurchase behavior.

My skin isn’t “glowing” or “revolutionized.” It’s just… calm. It’s not thirsty anymore. The dry patches on my cheeks? Gone. The sandpaper elbows? Managed. My hands are presentable. They look like hands that belong to a person who doesn’t work in a coal mine. It’s a low bar, but I’m clearing it now. I used to have this expensive lotion that smelled like roses and failure. It sat in a drawer. This jar of whipped beef fat with a pineapple vibe sits out. And gets used. Every day. I told my mom about it. She thought I was insane. Then she visited, tried it, and asked for the Etsy link. That’s the biggest endorsement I can give. My mom is skeptical of everything I buy online.

Would I buy it again? Yeah. I already did. I might get the unscented one next time too, just to try. But I’ll always have the pineapple one. It’s my favorite. It’s like the product works on two levels: the tallow fixes your skin, and the scent fixes your mood for ten seconds. It’s a good deal.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Weirdly, yes. From what I get, it’s similar to the oils our skin makes naturally. So it absorbs like it belongs there. It doesn’t just coat the surface. My face soaks it up and feels balanced, not greasy. It’s like giving your skin something it recognizes.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
Hasn’t clogged mine. And my skin can get fussy. Because it absorbs so well and matches our skin’s makeup, it doesn’t seem to just sit there and cause trouble. It’s not like slathering on Vaseline. It goes in. My pores seem fine with it. Better than fine.

**What does pineapple tallow balm smell like?**
Honestly? Just pineapple. Sweet, bright, fruity pineapple. Not artificial or overpowering. It smells exactly like you hope it would—like a fresh slice, not a candle or a candy. The smell doesn’t stick around on your skin, it’s just a nice little treat while you’re applying the balm.

Anyway. If your skin is being difficult, or dry, or just kinda sad, this might be worth a shot. The whole **tallow skincare** thing sounds odd but it’s oddly logical. And if you’re gonna try it, you might as well get the one that smells like a vacation. I got mine from that little Etsy shop. No regrets. Just smoother skin and a whiff of pineapple when I need it.
random_tangent: I should probably order another jar soon
